en: Mayon Volcano in Albay province is famous for its nearly perfect cone shape and is the most active volcano in the Philippines.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley into the Babuyan Channel.
The Philippine eagle is the national bird and is endemic only to the tropical forests of the Mindanao island group.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering an area of about 900 square kilometers in the CALABARZON region.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Philippine Sea is a large marginal sea located east and north of the archipelago in the western Pacific Ocean.
The Philippines is the top global producer of abaca, a banana plant whose strong fibers are used to make ropes and textiles.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site famous for its pristine coral reefs.
Due to its location in the Pacific typhoon belt, the Philippines experiences an average of twenty tropical cyclones annually.
Palawan is the largest island in the Mimaropa region and features the famous Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
Taal Volcano in Batangas is unique because its main crater is located inside a lake situated within a larger caldera.
